  • Reference
    • Find gaps in a foundation shade range

Compare a brand's shade mix with the market

brand_gaps.Rd

Splits shades into deep, medium and light bands and compares the share of a brand's shades in each band with the share across the whole market. Negative gaps show bands where the brand offers proportionally fewer shades than the market.

Usage

brand_gaps(shades, brand, breaks = c(0.45, 0.7))

Arguments

shades

A data frame with columns brand, product and lightness, such as foundation_shades. This is treated as the market.

brand

A single brand name, matching a value in shades$brand.

breaks

Two increasing numbers between 0 and 1 giving the lightness cut-offs between deep and medium, and between medium and light.

Value

A data frame with one row per band and columns:

band

Lightness band

brand_shades

Number of the brand's shades in the band

brand_share

Share of the brand's shades in the band

market_share

Share of all market shades in the band

gap

brand_share minus market_share; negative values mark under-represented bands

Examples

brand_gaps(foundation_shades, brand = "L'Oréal")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   band   brand_shades brand_share market_share     gap
#>   <fct>         <int>       <dbl>        <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 Deep             29       0.190        0.160  0.0297
#> 2 Medium           72       0.471        0.457  0.0138
#> 3 Light            52       0.340        0.383 -0.0435
# Negative gaps show where L'Oréal's range is thinner than the market's

brand_gaps(foundation_shades, brand = "FENTY BEAUTY by Rihanna")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   band   brand_shades brand_share market_share      gap
#>   <fct>         <int>       <dbl>        <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Deep             22       0.147        0.160 -0.0132 
#> 2 Medium           69       0.46         0.457  0.00325
#> 3 Light            59       0.393        0.383  0.00996
# Compare with a brand known for an inclusive shade range
